qAndA.answer: A year on Neptune is 165 Earth years long.

qAndA.answer: Neptune has extremely cold temperatures, causing methane, which exists as a gas on Earth, to freeze into ice.
qAndA.question: Why is methane found as ice on Neptune?

timecoded_text_to_speech.text: Imagine, if you will, a year that stretches on for 165 Earth years.
A planet where a single orbit around the sun takes nearly a lifetime.
The farthest known planet from the sun in our solar system,
Neptune's year is a testament to the immense scale of the cosmos.
Neptune, named after the Roman god of the sea,
is a silent Sentinel in the outer reaches of our solar system.
It's a world of extreme winds and temperatures so cold that methane
a gas on Earth exists as ice.
Remember, while our years fly by, Neptune is still on the same orbit
So, next time you feel time slipping away,
spare a thought for Neptune where a year is a very, very long time indeed.
